abstract: Oversees subglacial ice core access depth and bedrock profiling
system_message:
You are the Chief glaciologist (GLAC), responsible for overseeing subglacial ice core access depth and bedrock profiling across candidate polar drilling stations, as well as tracking ice deformation monitoring data.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Ice deformation monitoring（ICEFLOW）
information_points.content:
GLAC-ICEFLOW-9IG：Differential GPS tracking across the candidate surface perimeter at Wilkes Trough Ice Divide Station measures an annual horizontal ice flow velocity of 3 m/a.
GLAC-ICEFLOW-SHU：Twelve-month surface stake monitoring at Dome Charlie Traverse Camp shows an annual horizontal ice flow velocity of 6 m/a.
GLAC-ICEFLOW-P0C：Surface displacement surveys recorded by differential GPS stake arrays indicate an annual horizontal ice flow velocity of 9 m/a across the candidate perimeter of Amundsen Ridge Nunatak Outpost.

information_points.title: Oversees subglacial ice core access depth and bedrock profiling（CORE）
information_points.content:
GLAC-CORE-334：For Amundsen Ridge Nunatak Outpost, ice-penetrating radar sounding confirms a total bedrock access depth of 1,850 m from the surface snow level along the vertical trajectory to the basal ice-rock interface.
GLAC-CORE-FB0：According to the ice-penetrating radar survey for Dome Charlie Traverse Camp, the vertical borehole trajectory from the surface snow level to the subglacial bed yields a total bedrock access depth of 1,850 m.
GLAC-CORE-JFZ：Radar echo-sounding assessments at Wilkes Trough Ice Divide Station establish a total bedrock access depth of 2,400 m extending from the snow surface down to the basal interface.
